trial_court: Family Court, Gwalior, MISC. PETITION No. 6484 of 2023
facts_of_case: Marriage between petitioner and respondent was solemnized on 13.10.2019. Matrimonial dispute arose. Petitioner filed application for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act. Notice was issued against respondent, but she did not appear in court and trial proceeded ex-parte. Suit was decreed on 10.01.2023.

legal_principles.principle: Delay in filing an application under Order IX Rule 13 of CPC can be condoned if the delay is sufficiently explained.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, there is no error apparent on record caused by the Court below in allowing the application under Section 5 of Limitation Act.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure — Order IX Rule 13
cited_cases: Narmada Club & Anr. Vs. Shri P.K.Tare, 2004 (2) MPJR 315

legal_principles.principle: Notice under Order XIII of the Hindu Marriage Act must be served on the respondent in individual capacity.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, it cannot be assumed that respondent was served with notice. She came to know about the filing of divorce petition and subsequent order passed into it when she moved an application under Section 125 of Cr.P.C.

outcome.final_order: Family Court's order dated 07.10.2023 allowing respondent's application under Order IX Rule 13 of CPC is set aside.
